I will not spread myself too thin on 9 mu with only two people in the house. The wheat-maize rotation is still my main income, and with well irrigation I can push stable yield there, so I will keep most of the land in that system and only leave a small piece for cotton. I farm off last year's logic and then adjust for price and risk. Wheat and maize give me the steadiest return here in Quzhou. Cotton can still make money, but it eats labor and sprays, so I will only keep 1 mu of it to hold the crop and not let go of it completely. Because I finished high school and have farmed 40 years, I do not just copy one number every year. I look at fertilizer price, water, and target yield. Even so, I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, especially on wheat and maize. On the wheat-maize land I will feed wheat a bit heavier on nitrogen and phosphorus to secure tillers and grain, then push maize with more nitrogen and potassium because summer corn responds clearly if water is there. Cotton I will keep on a lighter area because it needs more watching, more topping, and more insect control. I will use improved or hybrid seed on all three crops, keep irrigation timely, and stay close to what has worked locally on fields that actually yield, not empty talk.
